Technical checks

2. Data & scope

Weekday morning turning volumes cover all 12 intersections, from the Midtown South study’s June 2024 collection campaign. Internal traffic flows balance. Roads are schematic; lanes, speeds and signal plans are assumed.

Field validation remains outstanding. Pedestrians, bicycles, bus stops and curbside obstruction are not modeled. No comparison against independently observed NYC travel times or queues has been completed.

NYC source study

3. Experimental method

Five controllers share the same traffic inputs. The fixed plan was selected from 16 candidates on separate development seeds. Each run contains three minutes of warm-up, ten minutes of demand and three minutes of drain.

Native Jev chooses hold or switch. Code enforces green durations of 22–60 seconds, three seconds of yellow and one second of all-red. Requests have a two-second deadline; late decisions are discarded and a queue-pressure rule provides fallback.

Bounded Jev selects a green split once per cycle: 47/35, 52/30 or 57/25 seconds for avenue/cross street. The 90-second cycle, coordination offsets and clearance times stay fixed. Changes expire each cycle; late or failed requests retain the baseline split. The original Jev controller and its recorded runs are preserved.

Confidence intervals describe variation across five paired seeds. They do not include all uncertainty in traffic behavior or establish effectiveness on actual streets.
